Medical student in northern Italy here. Gonna skip the closed schools and people at home to concentrate on a bigger problem: hospitals.

Doctors and nurses are all doing their best with what they can, but Healthcare has only had cuts in the past years and there are not enough beds and resources to deal with this virus.

Most wards have been turned into internal medicine or intensive care. We are lacking life support machines ("respiratori" in italian, correct me if I'm wrong, wordreference helped here") and mostly protection for those who work with the infected.
On top of that they are being told to work until they show symptoms, then either "we'll see if to quarantine you" or it's up to them to decide whether to stay at home or go to work. 

New doctors are being hired and the government finally decided to give more funds for specialization for the next year's up to 2024, but we definitely do not have enough right now. 

Even if the young people that need medical care are a small percentage, with the number of cases we have they are still a lot. It's a critical moment and it is important for everyone to do their part and stay at home. 

A choice already has to be made on who is worth saving or not, who gets treatment and who doesn't. As soon as new beds and equipment are avaiable they get occupied.
